links.comparator_used: Default 0.5 threshold versus F1-optimized thresholds set on the validation set for each model (LSTM 0.6463; GRU 0.7060; BiLSTM+Attention 0.5931)
links.outcome: Precision (PPV), recall and alert burden for seven-day-ahead agitation alerts
links.effect: Default thresholds gave 20–23% precision with 94–100% recall; optimized thresholds gave 73–82% precision with 56.25% recall (BiLSTM: accuracy 91.15%, F1 0.667). At test scale, optimized BiLSTM gave roughly one alert per 6–7 flagged days versus one per 2–3 under default, cutting expected false alarms by more than half.
links.tradeoff: Sensitivity fell from 94–100% at the default threshold to 56.25% at the optimized thresholds, so more agitation episodes are missed.
links.quote: Optimized thresholds raised precision to 73–82% with 56.25% recall (BiL-STM: accuracy 91.15%, F1 0.667).
